newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudan calls on U.N. to discuss Ethiopia attacks.
newsitem.headline: Sudan calls on U.N. to discuss Ethiopia attacks.

text.p: Sudan has called for an emergency session of the U.N. Security Council to take steps to prevent what it said were Ethiopian attacks on its territory.

Sudan radio said on Tuesday that Minister of Foreign Affairs Ali Osman Mohammad Taha urged the council in a message "to take steps to ensure that Ethiopia withdraws from positions inside Sudan and refrains from carrying out further attacks".
It said Sudan had asked for the emergency meeting to discuss its allegations that Ethiopia has attacked its territory, said the radio, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
The Sudanese government on Monday prepared public opinion for a military campaign after the army said Ethiopian forces had attacked two border towns.
"The message added...that the latest aggression was carried out in the wake of a number of violations which Ethiopia had carried out against Sudanese unity and security," the radio said.
"These aggressions, the message added, might bring the whole region closer to total war and might, in turn, jeopardize international peace and security," the radio said.
